**6B.10 Research Note: Olaf Scholz in 2024**

**Bottom line**
Partial yes. Scholz left ordinary people with somewhat better life chances on several fronts: inflation came down, wages and labor-market conditions were improving mid-year, and his budget/social-policy program targeted low earners, housing, children, regional equality, and access to jobs. But the year ended with recession, coalition collapse, and no-confidence defeat, so the improvement was real but fragile and incomplete.

**Accepted claims**
- **Bundesbank forecast for Germany: economy slowly regaining its footing** | Deutsche Bundesbank | 7 Jun 2024 | [URL](https://www.bundesbank.de/en/press/press-releases/bundesbank-forecast-for-germany-german-economy-slowly-regaining-its-footing-933658) | The Bundesbank said wage growth, falling inflation, and a stable labor market were helping households and that the economy was slowly regaining its footing. This is the strongest mid-2024 baseline evidence that ordinary people’s prospects were improving rather than deteriorating. | `6B.10` `6B.6`

- **Stable financial policy** | Federal Government | 24 Apr 2024 | [URL](https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-de/aktuelles/stable-financial-policy-2273918) | Scholz said fiscal policy was moving back toward debt-brake compliance while keeping high investment and raising growth potential. That suggests a medium-term attempt to improve life chances through a more sustainable macro framework, not just crisis spending. | `6B.10` `6B.9` `6B.4`

- **Bundeskanzler Scholz zum Haushaltsgesetz 2024** | Bundesregierung | 31 Jan 2024 | [URL](https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-de/service/newsletter-und-abos/bulletin/bundeskanzler-haushalt-2257440) | Scholz tied the budget to lower social-security contributions, higher housing benefit, higher child benefit, and the child supplement. This is direct evidence of improving ordinary households’ life chances through broad, rule-based support. | `6B.10` `6B.7` `6B.8`

- **Budget 2025 / growth initiative** | Federal Government | 5 Jul 2024 | [URL](https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-en/service/archive/budget-2025-2298116) | The government presented a 49-measure package with tax relief, social housing, infrastructure, renewables, and growth. That points to a program aimed at better living conditions and future earnings prospects for ordinary people. | `6B.10` `6B.9` `6B.7`

- **Bundestag: housing budget 2024** | Deutscher Bundestag | 19 Jan 2024 | [URL](https://www.bundestag.de/presse/hib/kurzmeldungen-987074) | The housing budget kept Wohngeld as the largest line item and added support for affordable housing and low-price construction. This is concrete evidence of improving access to shelter and reducing housing pressure on ordinary households. | `6B.10` `6B.7` `6B.2`

- **Bundestag: social cohesion and child support** | Deutscher Bundestag | 31 Jan 2024 | [URL](https://www.bundestag.de/dokumente/textarchiv/2023/kw27-de-regierungsbefragung-954170) | Scholz tied budget priorities to Bürgergeld, Wohngeld, higher child benefit, child supplement, and children’s basic security. That is direct support for children and low-income families, i.e. life chances beyond aggregate GDP. | `6B.10` `6B.8` `6B.7`

- **Day of German Unity 2024** | Federal Government | 3 Oct 2024 | [URL](https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-en/service/archive/federal-chancellor-day-of-unity-2313492) | Scholz said internal diversity is a strength and that politics should create equal living conditions across regions, including East-West equality. That is a direct equal-opportunity statement, not just macro welfare language. | `6B.10` `6B.8` `6B.3`

- **Girls’ Day at the Chancellery** | Bundesregierung | 23 Apr 2024 | [URL](https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-fr/service/archives/girls-day-2274468) | Scholz promoted girls in technical and scientific careers, which is concrete life-chance expansion rather than aggregate economic rhetoric. | `6B.10` `6B.8` `6B.3`

- **Scholz on disability rights** | Bundesregierung | 15 Sep 2024 | [URL](https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-de/service/newsletter-und-abos/bulletin/rede-von-bundeskanzler-olaf-scholz-2309098) | Scholz grounded disability policy in dignity and equal chances and called for self-determined lives for people with disabilities. This supports a claim that he tried to widen life chances for groups facing structural barriers. | `6B.10` `6B.8` `6B.3`

- **Scholz says Germany cannot stand by as Palestinians risk starvation** | Reuters | 16 May 2024 | [URL](https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/scholz-says-germany-cannot-stand-by-palestinians-risk-starvation-2024-05-16/) | Scholz pressed Netanyahu to improve aid access and said Palestinians in Gaza could not be left to starve. This is not domestic life-chance policy, but it is direct evidence of concern for avoiding mass civilian hardship. | `6B.10` `6B.6` `6B.8`

**Counterweights**
- **Germany’s GDP contracted in 2024** | Destatis | 15 Jan 2025 | [URL](https://www.destatis.de/EN/Press/2025/01/PE25_019_811.html) | GDP fell 0.2% in 2024. That is hard counterevidence against a strong claim that ordinary people’s life chances broadly improved across the year. | `6B.10`

- **Inflation averaged 2.2% in 2024** | Destatis | 16 Jan 2025 | [URL](https://www.destatis.de/EN/Press/2025/01/PE25_020_611.html) | Lower inflation helped households, but the fact that this is only a partial recovery metric shows the constraints remained substantial. It improves the baseline, but it does not prove a broad life-chance gain. | `6B.10` `6B.6`

- **German coalition collapses** | Reuters via Investing.com | 6 Nov 2024 | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/explainergerman-coalition-collapses-what-comes-next-3706936) | The coalition collapse created political chaos and weakened continuity, likely limiting delivery on social and housing gains late in the year. This is a real drag on translating policy into lived improvement. | `6B.10` `6B.9` `6B.5`

- **Bundestag no-confidence vote** | Deutscher Bundestag | 16 Dec 2024 | [URL](https://www.bundestag.de/dokumente/textarchiv/2024/kw47-vertrauensfrage-1030198) | Parliament’s loss of confidence confirmed year-end instability and policy discontinuity. That makes any life-chance improvement less durable and less confidently attributable to the chancellorship itself. | `6B.10` `6B.9`

- **Bürgergeld FAQ** | Bundesregierung | n.d. (active in 2024) | [URL](https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-de/aktuelles/faq-zum-buergergeld-2149774) | The rules allow reductions and, from 28 Mar 2024, even full cuts for persistent refusal to work. This is not proof of net harm, but it shows that some support was conditional rather than unconditional life-chance expansion. | `6B.10` `6B.7`

- **BND surveillance ruling** | Bundesverfassungsgericht | 8 Nov 2024 | [URL](https://www.bundesverfassungsgericht.de/SharedDocs/Pressemitteilungen/EN/2024/bvg24-093.html) | The Court found parts of the BND framework unconstitutional and oversight inadequate. That is a structural negative for a society in which ordinary people’s prospects and freedoms are fully protected. | `6B.10` `6B.9` `6B.8`

**Search gap**
The evidence is strongest for policies that could improve life chances and for mid-year macro improvement, but weaker on direct outcome attribution to Scholz personally. The biggest missing piece is causal proof that his 2024 measures materially improved lived mobility, income security, housing access, or regional opportunity by year-end despite the recession and coalition breakdown.
